title: Common Table Expressions (CTEs) & Recursive Queries
description: Write clean, modular SQL queries with WITH clauses, and traverse hierarchical trees and graphs with RECURSIVE CTEs.

data.text: A **Common Table Expression (CTE)** is a temporary result set defined within the execution scope of a single `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, or `DELETE` statement. Introduced via the `WITH` keyword, CTEs replace deeply nested subqueries with readable, sequential code.

data.title: Multi-Step Data Preparation with CTEs
data.content: Structuring complex reporting into readable stages.
data.code:
WITH regional_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        region,
        SUM(amount) AS total_sales,
        COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS active_customers
    FROM orders
    WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
    GROUP BY region
),
ranked_regions AS (
    SELECT 
        region,
        total_sales,
        active_customers,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC) AS sales_rank
    FROM regional_metrics
)
SELECT * FROM ranked_regions WHERE sales_rank <= 5;

data.text: Recursive CTEs for Tree & Graph Traversal

A **Recursive CTE** (`WITH RECURSIVE`) repeatedly evaluates a union between an initial base case (anchor member) and a recursive step (recursive member) until no new rows are produced. It is the gold standard for querying organizational hierarchies, category trees, and bill-of-materials.

data.title: Traversing an Employee Management Hierarchy
data.content: Recursively finding all subordinates under a specific director.
data.code:
WITH RECURSIVE org_chart AS (
    -- 1. Anchor Member: Base case (CEO or Department Head)
    SELECT id, name, manager_id, 1 AS depth
    FROM employees
    WHERE id = 'emp-ceo-001'

    UNION ALL

    -- 2. Recursive Member: Join employees to their managers in org_chart
    SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, oc.depth + 1
    FROM employees e
    INNER JOIN org_chart oc ON oc.id = e.manager_id
)
SELECT * FROM org_chart ORDER BY depth, name;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CTEs (`WITH`) make complex queries modular, readable, and maintainable.
Since PostgreSQL 12, non-recursive CTEs can be inlined by the optimizer by default for high performance.
Use `WITH RECURSIVE` to traverse organizational charts, folder hierarchies, and graph structures.
